note: Written on 2026-10-28, not found by the generator. A 30-hour constant test whose readings from the first hour on are in cells Excel shows as a clock (01:30), and from the 24th hour in cells formatted [h]:mm (24:00, 30:00), and its recovery the same way. openpyxl hands the Python reader a time and a duration, the browser's reader the text 01:30:00 and a date in January 1900. Both readers took the first number of a clock for the minutes, so 01:30 was minute 1 and the readings from the first hour on fell onto minutes 1 to 20, behind the first hour's: the test pumped for 45 minutes. A duration of a day or more was minute 1 in Python and was dropped in the browser. Both engines now read a clock as the hours and minutes it shows, and tests/test_ingestion.py holds this sheet to the times it records, not only the two engines to each other.
